hypothesis: At the existing simulated local water surfaces, does the southern missed component have a static terrain-accessible route, or is local head below all available sill routes?
baseline: round91 complete 5m event; no new hydraulic simulation
target: All 1457 cells in original round92 component2031, including every associated survey mark; all other original failures remain retained. This is post-result diagnosis, not a new validation scope.
bbox_basis: Original component bounding box plus100m each side; south clipped20m inside original domain. Fixed before this new diagnostic.
method: For each of all12 saved depth frames independently, seed every local cell with h>0.1 at its own eta=z+h. Propagate each constant seed stage through cardinal paths only where z+0.1<stage. At each cell retain highest accessible seed stage. Repeat once with asynchronous maximum-depth seeds, explicitly an optimistic diagnostic, never a simultaneous physical field. No friction, finite volume or travel time; result is potential static reachability only.
counterfactual: No extra head and no terrain edits; unlimited-volume constant-head propagation is a diagnostic relaxation, not a conservation-respecting flood model.
decision_rules: If no static route is available even under this relaxation, current local source stages and terrain do not permit this assumed static wet connection; this cannot distinguish wrong terrain from insufficient forcing.
If accessible but hydraulically missed, investigate time, volume, friction and transport before blaming a sealed terrain barrier. This is not proof of solver bug.
Snapshot absence cannot exclude between-frame transient opportunity; asynchronous maxima do not prove real concurrent supply.
No hydraulic candidate adopted without independent physical evidence. No change to88.56% or0.1m original scoring.
cost: Reuse12 fields and small crop; minutes, not a full rerun.
success: All1457target cells accounted, per-frame and max-only potential separated, algorithm independently verified on tiny synthetic cases and real target-component head thresholds.
reject: Input hash change, failed verification, or treating static reachability as actual flooding.
